auto.completedRanToAn: Completed ÷ ran to an end of their own (completed + failed + interrupted). What waits for you or is still running is not in the denominator: it has no result yet. For “filling in the form”, completed means that this run got the application submitted; a task that found the application already sent and did nothing counts neither as a success nor as a failure. This is the success rate of tasks, not what came of the applications: for that, see “Outcomes”.
auto.failedTheTaskStopped: Failed = the task stopped on an error of its own; interrupted = the program was closed during the task.
auto.byTheDayA: By the day a task started (local time). Click a legend entry to leave a series out.
auto.groupedByReasonMost: Grouped by reason, most frequent first
auto.howEachKindOf: How each kind of task did
auto.durationIsTheMedian: Duration is the median of tasks that finished or failed; AI cost is everything spent on that kind of task (failed runs included) over the ones that succeeded.
auto.theFiguresAboveCount: The figures above count runs; one application can take several (waiting for your answer, for your sign-in, going on after a budget). Here the runs of one application are taken together. Only applications that have come to a result are counted: one that waits for your answer or sign-in, or is still being worked, is in no denominator.
auto.applicationsBroughtToWhere: Applications brought to where one press sends them (or sent) ÷ (those + the ones that failed). Failed: the agent said it could not, it stopped at the same place several times, or the task ended in an error.
auto.ofThePreparedApplications: Of the prepared applications, those that got there without a question to you, without being stopped by you and without getting stuck. A sign-in only you can make is not counted.
auto.sentWithEvidenceOf: Sent, with evidence, of those to be sent
auto.ofTheApplicationsYou: Of the applications you approved, or that the agent sent itself under "send when nothing is open": those that are out with the confirmation page's words or a confirmation e-mail kept. Those still on their way are not counted.
auto.allRunsOfOne: All runs of one application together; only the prepared ones are counted.
auto.fromEachApplicationsOwn: From each application's own record of its runs. An application often takes several: waiting for your answer or sign-in, sending after approval, going on after being cut off. Every run after the first opens the browser again, finds its way back to the form and checks what the last one filled - that is "going over it again".
auto.stepsSpentGoingOver: Steps spent going over it again
auto.toolCallsOfEvery: Tool calls of every run after the first ÷ all tool calls. Lower is better: applications mostly done in one run, or taken up again without starting over.

mode.offHow: Doesn't look for updates. You can still check by hand.

mode.downloadHow: Also downloads and prepares it; you press Switch.
mode.autoHow: Also switches when idle (nothing applying or queued, nothing waiting for you in a kept window, no remote window open) within the hours below.

about.howSwitch: A switch is the tray app's restart: the database is backed up first, the new version is started, what is in progress finishes, and if the new version does not start the current one keeps running. The version before is kept so you can go back.
about.privacy: Looking for updates asks GitHub (api.github.com) for the list of releases; downloading fetches the package from github.com. Nothing about you is sent. A package is checked against its SHA-256 checksum and thrown away if it does not match; nothing in it is run.
